text:
amal: Heads up — I found a debug bundle uploaded to gs://redwood-dev-artifacts/debug-bundles/2026-03-23/instance-42.tar.gz that contains a VAULT_TOKEN and a GCP service account key file. Marking this P0 for secret rotation and containment :rotating_light:

security-bot: Incident INC-2026-145 created (severity: high). Notifying oncall.

marta: Ugh. Can you paste the bundle path + a quick grep snippet (mask values) so we can triage scope?

amal: Path above. Grep output (masked):

```
VAULT_TOKEN=***vault-token-xxxx***
# found in: instance-42/debug/env
GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/tmp/sa-key.json
{"type": "service_account", "project_id": "redwood-dev", "private_key_id": "***", "private_key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n***\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----"}
# found in: instance-42/debug/sa-key.json
```

amal: I did NOT paste the raw token or key here. I also verified the bundle lifecycle policy is 30d (too long) and the bucket is public to the org with a few external members.

darius: Thanks Amal. Suggested containment + rotation playbook: 1) Revoke VAULT token accessor immediately. 2) Force tailing leases and revoke any active Vault tokens for that accessor. 3) Revoke/delete the SA key and create a new one with minimal scopes. 4) Rewrap any ciphertext created by old KMS key (if in use) and consider rekeying transit. 5) Tighten bucket ACL + add retention TTL to 24h. 6) Enable verbose audit logging for Vault for 7d.

jonathan: Agree. Who can run the gcloud/key revoke? ops-oncall? Also we should check if the token was used to read any high-sensitivity paths (kv/data/prod-*).

ops-oncall: I can run revokes now. Steps I'm about to execute:

```
# revoke vault token by accessor
vault token-revoke -accessor "***accessor***"  # placeholder used here
# remove SA key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=debug-sa@redwood-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-dev
# create new key with restricted roles
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create new-sa-key.json --iam-account=debug-sa@redwood-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-dev
```

ops-oncall: Done (commands executed). Put new key into a short-lived secret in Vault with policy 'debug-limited'.

marta: I'll run a quick audit query on Vault and GCP logs for the last 48h to see read activity from that token/SA.

amal: Quick results: vault audit shows 3 token-lookup calls from instance-42 in the last 12h, and one KV read under path secret/data/dev/feature-flags (low sensitivity). No reads under secret/data/prod. GCP audit shows the SA was used to upload the bundle to that bucket 2026-03-23T03:12Z.

darius: Good catch. Still proceed with rewrap/rotate transit key for that service so old ciphertext can't be decrypted if keys were exfiltrated. Also add an allowlist so debug SA cannot access prod buckets.

jonathan: I'll submit a quick RBAC change: remove storage.objectAdmin from debug-sa and grant storage.objectCreator/store.objectViewer limited to debug bucket only. Will push as an ACL patch and request review.

marta: Audit logging plan: enable full Vault audit sink (json) -> central S3/GCS for 7 days, then index in Splunk. Also enable GCP object access logs on that bucket and set retention.

amal: Action items and owners:
- revoke token + delete old SA key (ops-oncall) — done
- create new SA key scoped to debug bucket (ops-oncall) — done
- rotate Vault transit key / rewrap ciphertext (darius) — started
- RBAC scoping for debug-sa (jonathan) — in PR
- enable Vault/GCP audit sinks + 7d retention (marta) — in progress
- change bucket lifecycle to 24h TTL and block public access (jonathan) — in PR

security-bot: Audit trail linked: https://internal.incidents/INC-2026-145 (log ids attached).

ops-oncall: Ran `vault token-revoke` and `gcloud iam keys delete`. Confirmed key deletion response OK.

darius: Rewrap status: rewrap completed for objects that used legacy-KMS-01. Creating ticket to rekey transit-KMS-02 next maintenance window (ETA: 6h).

marta: Audit queries done — no prod reads, but there were two attempts to access partner-integration secrets (denied). I'll set an alert for any denied->allowed transitions.

jonathan: PR merged for RBAC scoping + bucket policy. Lifecycle changed to 24h and uniform bucket-level access enabled.

amal: Thanks team. Postmortem: we'll run a 1hr blameless review tomorrow 11:00 PT to cover how debug bundles get created and why they contained env/keys. Recommend: default debug agent should scrub env files and never upload credential files.

marta: +1. I'll schedule and invite infra, devex, security.

amal: Closing thread for now; updating INC-2026-145 with actions and owners. :white_check_mark:
